stem.text: The name ‘chlorate’ is used for an anion consisting of chlorine and oxygen only.
In a molecule of $\text{ICl}$, the iodine atom has oxidation number $x$ and the chlorine atom has oxidation number $y$.
When $\text{ICl}$ is added to $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, iodine is reduced.
Which statement about the value of $x$ or $y$ is correct?

A.text: $x$ is the same as the oxidation number of $\text{Cl}$ in the chlorate ion formed when $\text{Cl}_2\text{(aq)}$ is added to cold $\text{NaOH(aq)}$.

B.text: $x$ is the same as the oxidation number of $\text{Cl}$ in the chlorate ion formed when $\text{Cl}_2\text{(aq)}$ is added to hot $\text{NaOH(aq)}$.

C.text: $y$ is the same as the oxidation number of $\text{Cl}$ in the chlorate ion formed when $\text{Cl}_2\text{(aq)}$ is added to cold $\text{NaOH(aq)}$.

D.text: $y$ is the same as the oxidation number of $\text{Cl}$ in the chlorate ion formed when $\text{Cl}_2\text{(aq)}$ is added to hot $\text{NaOH(aq)}$.
